title: Beyond the Clipboard, Designing a Better Observation Tool
author: Allison Schultz
summary: Teacher observation forms often constrain rather than enhance coaching conversations because they impose someone else's framework and rubric definitions rather than serving the observer's actual instructional priorities. To solve this problem, Schultz created The Nest Navigator, a simple observation guide that operationalizes five core teaching questions into concrete, observable teaching moves while reducing unconscious bias. The tool explicitly surfaces what the observer is and isn't noticing, inviting richer coaching conversations grounded in a fuller, more balanced picture of classroom instruction.
points: Pre-made observation forms create a false sense of objectivity but force observers to guess at definitions and conceptualizations they don't share with the teacher.
Observers naturally gravitate toward their own trained biases, noticing the same teaching moves repeatedly while missing other important dynamics of effective instruction.
The Nest Navigator operationalizes five essential coaching questions into specific, observable look-fors with checkbox prompts that cue noticing of diverse teaching behaviors.
Absences on the observation tool become conversation triggers rather than judgment points, supporting a forward-looking coaching stance focused on growth.
quotes: What if the tools we use to observe teachers are the very things constraining the quality of our feedback? When they're good, they're genuinely energizing, windows into the craft, the chemistry, and the surprising moments that make classrooms breathe. I wrestled with these things not because I didn't understand their importance in the classroom, but I didn't know how she was conceptualizing them. Like a teacher teaching from a scripted lesson, my feedback to her lacked a certain authenticity.
Research shows that teachers often default to calling on one eager student who can provide the correct answer and then move on, assuming the rest of the class is equally ready to proceed.
Ultimately, The Nest Navigator helps me capture a fuller, more nuanced picture of what's unfolding in the classroom without relying solely on what my eyes are already trained to notice.
A big part of my motivation for creating The Nest Navigator was to reduce my own biases during classroom observations.” Archived from Episcopal Academy CTL on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
